thread.title: Indexes Mixed As S&P 500 Today Climbs While Tech Stocks Struggle | Investor's Business Daily

author: JUAN CARLOS ARANCIBIA
title: Indexes Mixed As S&P 500 Today Climbs While Tech Stocks Struggle | Investor's Business Daily
text:
The weight of Amazon.com ( AMZN ) and Apple ( AAPL ) on the stock market became all too obvious Monday, as those two stocks caused much of the suffering on the Nasdaq composite. But the S&P 500 today climbed.
X The Nasdaq, where Apple has the greatest weighting, was down 0.2% after paring losses. The composite earlier was down as much as 1.4%.
Apple shares slid 3% after a report that the company halted plans to increase production lines for the iPhone XR. Also, Rosenblatt Securities downgraded the stock. Nomura set a 185 price target on Apple, which is 9% below the current share price. Apple stock is close to erasing all gains from the 194.30 buy point of a breakout in July.
Amazon.com was down 2% after it announced it will offer free shipping on all holiday orders , not just its Prime members. Amazon shares hit resistance at the 200-day moving average Friday and weak action continued with Monday's drop.
The S&P 500 today climbed 0.7% and the Dow Jones industrial average added 0.9%. The energy sector led the market after the price of crude climbed 0.5% to $63.50 a barrel as the commodity tries to end a monthlong swoon.
Stock Market Today: REITs Rally Building, tobacco, utility and real estate investment trust (REIT) industry groups were among Monday's leaders. Technology made up the weakest portions of the market, with semiconductor, networking, internet and some software groups in the bottom 20 of 197 groups.
The IBD 50 — still heavy with technology stocks — was down 0.6% in afternoon trading. But Health Insurance Innovations ( HIIQ ) was the biggest loser, down 15% in big volume. The stock is sinking toward its 200-day line.
The company said Friday it had terminated its relationship with Simple Health, an insurance distributor that came under an action from the Federal Trade Commission. The FTC said a federal judge temporarily shut down Simple Health over deceptive practices. Health Insurance Innovations said Simple Health handled less than 10% of its policies and it does not expect a negative impact on its outlook.
Several REITs have emerged in today's IBD 50, and three of them had the best performances: Medical Properties Trust ( MPW ), Sabra Healthcare ( SBRA ) and CareTrust REIT ( CTRE ). The latter two are forming bases. REITs are drawing interest from investors because they provide dividends that can offset or mitigate losses in share prices.
